title: Adding a review comment is allowed for policy.approve holders who lack policy.update (PM-L02 fix regression guard)
description: policy.routes.js POST /:policyId/comments deliberately uses requireAnyPermission(['policy.update','policy.approve']) instead of requirePermission('policy.update') alone, per code comment PM-L02 — a reviewer's real permission set is typically policy.approve WITHOUT policy.update. Verifies this intentional broadening still holds and hasn't regressed to policy.update-only.
preconditions: User has policy.approve but NOT policy.update
steps: As the policy.approve-only user, POST /policies/:policyId/comments with a comment body
expectedResult: Comment is created successfully (201/200), not rejected with 403 — this reviewer role must be able to annotate policies mid-review without edit rights.

title: A policy's own creator can approve/transition their own draft with no self-review prevention check found in policy.service.js transition()
description: policy.service.js's transition(policyId, targetState, userId, opts) has no visible check comparing userId against the policy's createdBy/author before allowing a state transition guarded only by requirePermission('policy.approve') at the route level. Unlike the evidence-management module's mapping self-review guard, no equivalent author != approver check was found here — flag as a gap pending confirmation.
preconditions: User A holds policy.approve and created (createdBy) a draft policy P
steps: As User A, POST /policies/P/transition targeting the next workflow state (e.g. draft -> review, or review -> approved if User A also has the right role)
expectedResult: Document actual behavior: if the transition succeeds without a distinct second reviewer, this confirms the self-review gap — the policy's own author can approve their own document, unlike segregation-of-duties patterns enforced elsewhere in the platform (e.g. evidence-mapping). Should be flagged for remediation if confirmed.

title: Hard delete is rejected for a policy not in draft or archived status
description: policy.controller.js hardDelete enforces: "Only 'draft' or 'archived' policies may be hard-deleted — archive it first via the workflow transition."
steps: DELETE /policies/:policyId/permanent on a policy currently in 'active' status
expectedResult: Request is rejected (400/409) with a message requiring the policy to be draft or archived first — an active/approved policy can never be permanently destroyed directly.

title: AI-generated policy content is rendered without executing embedded script via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
preconditions: A policy's AI-generated or AI Reader content field contains an injected <script> or onerror= payload (simulated via direct DB edit or AI generation prompt injection)
steps: Open the policy detail/reader view that renders the content via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
expectedResult: Content is sanitized before render (e.g. DOMPurify or equivalent) — no script executes and no XSS occurs, despite the use of dangerouslySetInnerHTML in the renderer.

title: GET /policies/:policyId rejects a policyId belonging to another organization
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) each with a policy
Valid JWT for a user in org A
steps: As an org A user, call GET /policies/:policyId using org B's policy ID
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403/404 — no policy content, control mappings, or version history from org B is returned.

title: Public/unauthenticated template listing endpoint enforces a rate limit
preconditions: A public (unauthenticated) template endpoint is exposed, if one exists outside router.use(authenticate) in policy.routes.js
steps: Send 100+ rapid sequential requests to the public template endpoint from a single IP
expectedResult: Requests beyond the configured rate limit are throttled (429), preventing scraping/DoS of the public template catalog.
